title: EU soft-fencing routing and customer exemption protocol
creator: Marina Lopez
description:
Summary: Implement a ‘soft-fencing’ routing mode for EU data constraints that balances strict residency requirements with operational availability. Soft-fencing prefers EU-hosted model variants and paths, but allows auditable, time-limited non-EU fallback when strict routing would cause outage or SLA breaches.

Goals:
- Provide three per-customer policy modes: strict (fail-fast for non-EU paths), soft-fence (prefer EU, allow fallback with audit and TTL), permissive (best-effort routing).
- Enforce allowlist/denylist at the customer level for both regions and model variants; allow scoped exemptions via a signed customer exemption token.
- Add Consent-Header evaluation and a runtime decision flag that can be overridden only via signed escape tokens or emergency operator flow.
- Emit telemetry and billing tags for any non-EU fallbacks and provide an alerting surface for elevated fallback rates.

Design/behavior notes:
- Routing decision evaluation order: 1) Customer policy (strict/soft/permissive) 2) Tenant-level allow/deny lists 3) Consent header and signed exemption tokens 4) Capacity-aware tier routing (dedicated -> hosted) 5) Fallback variant selection (EU-quantized -> global-quantized).
- Soft-fence fallback mechanics: when an EU-only candidate set has no healthy endpoints within latency/throughput SLOs, mark request as a ‘soft-fence-fallback’. Attach a 1-hour TTL audit entry and tag tokens with fallback_reason, fallback_region, and operator_id if applicable. Fallbacks are only allowed up to a configured rate per-customer (default 0.5% of routed requests).
- Exemption tokens: short-lived JWT signed by customer or Redwood support. Token contains fields: customer_id, scope (region/model), expires_at, issuance_reason. At runtime we validate signature and check revocation list.
- Auditing: every non-EU fallback must create an immutable audit row with request_id, customer_id, decision_path, token_used (if any), and snapshot URL to request trace. Audit rows are retained per customer policy but default 365 days for EU-sensitive customers.

Implementation components:
- Policy engine extension: new policy mode field + allow/deny set evaluation. This is a small change to the decision graph in policy-service.
- Router runtime: add soft-fence flag to routing context, implement fallback counter and TTL metadata in the request envelope.
- Token service: lightweight verifier + revocation table in control plane, support for cryptographic attestation header.
- Console: per-customer toggle for soft-fence, UI shows fallback rate, recent audit entries, and manual revoke button for exemption tokens.
- Observability: dashboard with non-EU-fallback-rate (p95), alert when >0.1% for strict customers or >1% for soft-fence customers over 5m.

Constraints & tradeoffs:
- Allowing fallback increases risk surface for EU-sensitive data; mitigate with mandatory audit and quick-revocation mechanism.
- Strict mode increases availability risk for customers in geographic outage scenarios; soft-fence is a compromise but adds complexity to billing and SLAs.
- Performance impact: additional policy checks and JWT validations add ~0.5ms median to request decision path; we will micro-optimize by caching verified tokens for their TTL.

Acceptance criteria (see field acceptance_criteria): implementation behind feature flag, exercised by integration tests and chaos scenario that simulates EU region capacity outages, console toggle available, alerting wired up, security review completed.
acceptance_criteria: Feature gated behind feature flag and disabled by default
Per-customer policy modes configurable via Console and API
Non-EU fallbacks emit audit entries with required metadata
Exemption tokens validated and revocable via control plane
Integration tests cover strict/soft/permissive flows and emergency fallback
Metrics and alerting for fallback rates deployed to production graph
Security review approval attached to ticket
rollout_plan: Dev: unit tests + local policy-service sim (branch)
Canary: enable feature flag for internal alpha customers (1%) for 48h
Gradual: expand to 5%/20% with monitoring gates at each step
Beta: opt-in for select EU customers with explicit SLA and support agreement
GA: flip default behavior for new customers to soft-fence; existing customers unchanged
